opening.argument: The speaker explicitly warns viewers not to visit the websites or download the files, and says the interactions took place in a carefully controlled sandbox. The payment offer for a game review and the downloaded archive are presented as subjects of investigation, not as an invitation to take part. The account then describes a request to disable antivirus protection, while an antivirus warning appears alongside the files. The speaker also reports that malware analysis characterized the examined file as credential-stealing spyware. These details support a warning about the purported crypto-game promotion. They do not show that viewers were encouraged to accept the offer, nor do they establish that anyone suffered a loss.

citations.quote: Don't try to go to any of these websites yourself or download any of this stuff.
Every interaction that I had with this site was in a carefully controlled sandbox environment
They then asked me to disable my antivirus, and assured me it was completely safe.
Reading through the Malware Analysis Report, it seems that this is guaranteed to be Spyware. Specifically, one that steals your credentials stored in files on your computer
